prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: production background bitmap for a French illustrated PC-style management game, Le Placard.
Input image 1 is the exact editable game-room geometry to preserve. Input image 2 is a supporting art-direction reference only: warm Breton craft village, aged stone, forest green, amber lamps and carefully painted surfaces.
Primary request: give the first warehouse soul and a lived-in, hand-crafted illustrated-game feel. Preserve the exact top-down orthographic camera, rectangular room footprint and door opening at bottom centre; output 1536x1024 landscape. No perspective tilt. The interior playable floor must remain open and fully readable in the exact rectangle x=168 through 1368, y=120 through 870. All props must sit strictly OUTSIDE that rectangle, inside perimeter strips only.
Art direction: a lovingly maintained Breton artisan workshop at late afternoon, richly painted game art, confident fine outlines, attractive deep forest-green metal, warm weathered grey stone, honey-coloured timber trim, amber practical lights. Patinated walls, rivets, copper pipes and neatly routed cables, small pegboard tools, folded work apron, a coffee mug on a tiny wall shelf, delivery slips and a discreet vintage workshop plaque at the perimeter. Natural wear with personality, not dirty dereliction. Some ivy and plants outside the building perimeter, restrained. Keep all furniture at the perimeter.
Floor: medium warm grey concrete with fine grain, subtle worn patches, faint long scuff marks and soft light pools from the walls; quiet even texture that still looks good zoomed in. No giant floor lettering, no gameplay grid baked into the bitmap, no crops, no grow lamps, no storage racks or machines on playable floor, no UI, no stats, no watermark.
Lighting: inviting local amber lamp light and a restrained cool teal shadow contrast, enough illumination to read interactive objects to be added later. Maintain edges exactly for existing game grid alignment. This is a real final game asset, not a screenshot mockup.
